owner.occupation: Coordinator at a community Men's Shed

world.bio: Retired schoolteacher, thirty-one years teaching maths and woodwork in Coburg and Preston. Now I coordinate a community Men's Shed in Melbourne's northern suburbs, keeping it running on grants, sausage sizzles and patience. About sixty members, mostly retirees, a few men dealing with loneliness or depression who find the Shed easier than a clinic.
skills_assets: A brick building in Preston with a main workshop, a small kitchen and a meeting room
Thirty-one years of teaching and community leadership
Council grant for a woodworking program that pairs retirees with apprentices
Sixty members with a wide range of skills, from retired plumbers to former bank managers
Weekly sausage sizzle at the Bunnings, raising about $600 a month
Relationship with the local council's community development officer
Caravan and a plan to travel to Queensland after the program

projects.name: Woodworking program
projects.text: The Shed won a council grant for a woodworking program pairing retirees with apprentices, from November to January. The grant requires a qualified cabinetmaker to supervise, and nobody on the roster qualifies. The program needs an experienced woodworker and the grant says the supervisor must hold an Australian Cert III in Cabinet Making.

projects.name: Empty back half
projects.text: The back half of the Shed's building has stood empty since the bike co-op moved out. About 90 square metres, concrete floor, roller door. I'd like to put it to use but we've got no plan or money.

projects.name: Caravan trip
projects.text: Planning to go up to Queensland for six weeks in February with my wife Lorraine.

notes.text: Tuesday morning at the Shed. Eight men, three teas, one broken drill press. Frank fixed it with a bit of wire and swearing. We call that maintenance.

Good news and bad news. The council confirmed the grant: $38,000 for the woodworking program with apprentices. Bad news: clause 4.2 says the supervisor must hold Cert III in Cabinet Making. I read it twice, thinking maybe 'or equivalent'. It doesn't say that.

Went through the roster. Plumbers, electricians, a retired vet, two bank managers, a man who used to make violins. Not one Cert III cabinetmaker. We have plenty of people who can build a bookshelf, but the grant wants paper.
The back half of the building is empty. Sat in it for ten minutes. You can hear the roller door rattling in the wind. Thought about what a proper bench and four vices would do there.
Grandson's first footy game. Under-8s. He ran in the wrong direction twice. I cheered loudly each time. His mother said I'm embarrassing. I said I'm a grandfather.
Lorraine asked if we're still going to Queensland. I said the caravan is serviced, I just need to find someone to run the program. She looked at me and said, 'You always find someone'.
Tried making sourdough. The loaf could stop a door. Lorraine says I should take it to the Shed and use it as a workbench weight.
Called the council officer, Priya. She said the grant is secure but the conditions are firm. I asked if there's flexibility. She said she'd check. She didn't sound hopeful.

Posted a call in our newsletter for any qualified cabinetmakers, retired or not. Three replies so far: one wanted to help but is in Perth, one lacks the certificate, one just wanted to know if the Shed has a pool table.

messages.text: Priya: The grant conditions are as written. The supervisor needs a Cert III. Graham: Understood. Priya: Let me know if you find someone. Graham: I'm looking.
Frank: What's the plan for the program? Graham: We need a qualified cabinetmaker. Frank: I know a few retired chippies but none of them have the paper. Graham: Paper is the issue.
Lorraine: Dinner at 6. Graham: I'll be late. Lorraine: Of course. Graham: I'm sorry. Lorraine: Bring the bread.
Ollie: Grandpa, did you see my goal? Graham: I did. Ollie: It was an own goal. Graham: Still a goal.
Reader: I can build cabinets but no certificate. Graham: Thanks for offering. Reader: Does that matter? Graham: Sadly yes.

relations.about: Council community development officer, supportive but rule-bound.
Longtime Shed member, retired plumber, good with tools.

constraints: Grant requires supervisor with Australian Cert III in Cabinet Making
Program must run November to January
Insurance only covers supervised use of heavy tools
sensitive: Worries the program will collapse and the grant be withdrawn

disclosure_policy.t0_public: Coordinator of a community Men's Shed; the back half of the building is empty; a new woodworking program runs from November to January and needs an experienced woodworker.
